Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 62, verse 1–4:

﴿Al-Quddus (the All-Holy)﴾ This was mentioned in al-Hashr [24]. ﴿It is He who raised among the unlettered (al-ummiyyin) a messenger from among themselves﴾, meaning our master Muhammad (ﷺ). Al-ummiyyin are the Arabs, and the meaning of ummi (unlettered) has been mentioned in al-A'raf [157]. ﴿And others from among them﴾ is in conjunction with al-ummiyyin. By these others he meant Persia. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked: "Who are these others?" He placed his hand on Salman al-Farisi and said: "If knowledge were at the Pleiades, men from these would attain it," meaning Persia. It was also said that they are the Romans. The word ﴿from them﴾ on these two opinions means in humanity and in religion, not in lineage. It was also said: they are the people of Yemen. It was said: they are the Successors (al-tabi'un). It was said: they are all the Muslims. The first opinion is more preponderant because it is related in the authentic hadith. ﴿Who have not yet joined them﴾, meaning: those who have not yet joined them, in negation, and they will join them. This is because ﴿lamma﴾ refers to the recent past up to the present. ﴿That is the bounty of Allah﴾ refers to the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ) and the guidance of people through him.

**Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on Surah al-Jumu'ah, verses 5–6:**

﴿The likeness of those who were charged with the Torah﴾ means the Jews. The meaning of "were charged with the Torah" is that they were obligated to act upon it and to carry out its commands and prohibitions. ﴿Then they did not bear it﴾ means they did not obey its command and did not act upon it. God likened them to a donkey that carries books on its back while not knowing what is in them. ﴿Wretched is the likeness of the people who denied the signs of God﴾ means the Jews who denied our master Muhammad (ﷺ). They are the ones who were charged with the Torah but did not bear it, because the Torah speaks of his prophethood (ﷺ). Whoever reads it and does not believe in him has contradicted the Torah. ﴿So wish for death﴾ has been mentioned in al-Baqarah [94].

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 62, verse 9–10:

﴿When the call is made for prayer on the day of Friday, then hasten to the remembrance of Allah﴾ The "call for prayer" (al-nida' li-l-salah) is the adhan (call to prayer) for it. The word "min" in His words ﴿on the day of Friday﴾ explains "idha" (when) and clarifies it. "The remembrance of Allah" is intended to mean the khutbah (sermon) and the prayer. Eight issues are connected to this verse:

The first: Scholars differ regarding the adhan for Friday: is it a sunnah like the adhan for the other prayers, or is it obligatory? The apparent meaning of the verse suggests the latter, since hastening to it is conditioned on the adhan, and hastening is obligatory, so the adhan is obligatory.

The second: The adhan for Friday, at the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, was on the wall of the mosque. It was also said: at the door of the mosque. And it was said: it was before him ﷺ while he was on the minbar (pulpit). The Umayyads followed this practice, and it remained in Cordoba for a time, and it still remains in the East to this day. Abu Muhammad ibn al-Faras said: Malik said in al-Majmu'ah that Hisham ibn Abd al-Malik was the one who introduced the adhan before him (the imam). He said: This is evidence that the hadith on this matter is weak.

The third: The adhan for Friday was originally one call. Then Uthman (may Allah be pleased with him) added a call at al-Zawra' so that the people would hear it. The jurists differed over whether it is recommended that two or three adhans be called for it.

The fourth: The "sa'y" (hastening) in the verse means walking, not running. Umar ibn al-Khattab recited: "fa-amdu ila dhikr Allah" (then proceed to the remembrance of Allah), and this is an explanation of sa'y. It differs from the sa'y in the words of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "When the iqamah is called for prayer, do not come to it while you are hurrying (tas'awn)."

The fifth: Attending Friday prayer is obligatory, since the command in the verse is by consensus taken to mean obligation. However, it is not obligatory on women, children, or the sick, by consensus, nor on the slave or the traveler according to Malik and the majority; in contrast to the Zahiriyyah, who held onto the general wording of the verse. The majority's evidence is the words of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "Friday prayer is obligatory upon every Muslim in congregation, except four: a owned slave, a woman, a child, or a sick person." Their evidence regarding the traveler is that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not establish Friday prayer while travelling. Scholars differed over whether Friday prayer is dropped due to rain, and whether it is permissible for the bridegroom (al-arus) to be absent from it. The well-known view is that it is not dropped for him, due to the generality of the verse.

The sixth: Scholars differed over when coming to the prayer becomes binding. It was said: when the sun passes its zenith. It was said: when the muezzin calls the adhan, and this is the apparent meaning of the verse.

The seventh: Scholars differed over the distance from which hastening to Friday prayer is obligatory. It was said: three miles, which is the view of Malik. It was said: six miles. It was said: it is obligatory upon whoever is within the town (misr). It was said: upon whoever hears the call. It was said: upon whoever the night brings back to his family.

The eighth: Scholars differed over whether the ruler (al-wali) is a condition for Friday prayer or not, in two opinions. The well-known view is that he is not a condition, because Allah did not stipulate him in the verse.

﴿And leave off trade﴾ This is a command to abandon trading on Friday when the muezzins begin the adhan, and this is obligatory; it therefore requires the prohibition of trade. Scholars differed over whether a sale concluded at that time is annulled or not. They also differed over whether the sale by those not obligated to attend Friday prayer, such as women and slaves, is permissible at that time or not. The more apparent view is that it is permissible, since it is only prohibited for those who are called to Friday prayer.

﴿Then disperse in the land﴾ This command is one of permission, by consensus. Ibn Atiyyah and Ibn al-Faras reported consensus on this.

﴿And seek of the bounty of Allah, and remember Allah much that you may succeed﴾ It was said: its meaning is seeking livelihood, so the command here is one of permission. It was reported from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "The bounty sought is visiting the sick, or keeping ties with a friend, or following a funeral." It was also said: it is seeking knowledge. And if the hadith is authentic, one should not turn away from it to anything else.

﴿But when they see a trade or a diversion, they rush off to it﴾. The occasion of revelation was that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was standing on the minbar (pulpit) delivering the khutbah (sermon) on Friday, when a caravan arrived from Syria carrying food. Its leader was Dihya ibn Khalifa al-Kalbi. It was their custom that when a caravan entered Madinah it did so with drums and shouting, out of joy at its arrival. When the caravan entered in this way, the people in the mosque broke away toward it and left the Messenger of God (ﷺ) standing on the minbar. Only twelve men remained with him. Jabir ibn Abdullah said: "I was one of them." Some reported that among them were the ten who were given the good news of Paradise. People differed about the twelfth: it was said to be Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, and it was said to be Ammar ibn Yasir. It was also said that only eight remained with him (ﷺ). It is related that he (ﷺ) said to those who remained: "Indeed, the stones would have been hurled down upon those who broke away." The apparent meaning of the verse implies that a congregation is a condition for the Jumu'ah (Friday congregational prayer), which is the view of Malik and the majority of scholars. However, they differed over the minimum number of people by whom the Jumu'ah is validly established. Malik said: there is no fixed number; rather, they are a group sufficient for a village to be inhabited by them. Ibn al-Majishun related from Malik that the number is thirty. Al-Shafi'i said: forty. Abu Hanifa said: three, together with the imam. It was also said: twelve, the number of those who remained with the Prophet (ﷺ).

If it is asked: why did He say "they broke away to it" with a singular pronoun, when trade and diversion have both been mentioned? The answer has two aspects. The first is that He meant that they broke away to the diversion and broke away to the trade, and then deleted one of them because the other indicates it. This was stated by al-Zamakhshari. The second is that He used the singular because He was giving precedence to trade, since it was more important, and it was the cause of the diversion, whereas the diversion was not the cause of it. This was stated by Ibn 'Atiyya.

﴿And they left you standing﴾. Scholars differed over whether standing during the khutbah is obligatory or not, and if it is obligatory, whether it is a condition of the khutbah or not. Whoever holds it obligatory and a condition takes the apparent meaning of the verse, which mentions standing. Whoever does not hold it obligatory sees that what the Prophet (ﷺ) did in this regard was not obligatory. The position of Malik is that it is part of the Sunnah of the khutbah to sit before it and to sit between the two khutbahs. Abu Hanifa said: one does not sit between the two khutbahs, on the apparent meaning of the verse, which mentions standing in it but not sitting. The proof for Malik is the practice of the Messenger of God (ﷺ).

﴿Say: What is with God is better than diversion and than trade﴾. If it is asked: why did He put diversion before trade here, while He put trade before diversion in the previous verse? The answer: each of the two places came in the way that suits it. This is because the Arabs sometimes begin with the greater and then descend to the lesser, as when you say: "So-and-so betrays in the much and the little," where you began with the much and then added betrayal in what is less. And sometimes they begin with the lesser and then ascend to the greater, as when you say: "So-and-so is trustworthy in the little and the much," where you began with the little and then added trustworthiness in what is more. Had you reversed either of these two examples, it would not have been good. For if in betrayal you had mentioned the little first, it would be understood that he betrays in the much, a fortiori. And if in trustworthiness you had mentioned the much first, it would be understood that he is trustworthy in the little, a fortiori, so mentioning it afterward would serve no purpose. Likewise is His saying: ﴿But when they see a trade or a diversion, they rush off to it﴾. He placed trade first here to show that they break away to it, and that, along with that, they break away to the diversion, which is lower than it. And His saying: ﴿better than diversion and than trade﴾ places diversion first to show that what is with God is better than diversion, and that it is also better than trade, which is greater than it. Had either of the two places been reversed, it would not have been fitting.
